### Problem: Implement a queue using two stacks {#sec-cx-p3-queue}

::: {.p-statement}
Implement a FIFO queue with `push`, `pop`, `peek` and `empty`, using only stack operations (push to top, pop from top, peek top, size). Every operation should be amortized $O(1)$.

Source: [LC 232 · Implement Queue using Stacks](https://leetcode.com/problems/implement-queue-using-stacks/){.solved difficulty="Easy"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Push onto an `inbox` stack. To pop, take from an `outbox` stack; when the outbox is empty, pour the whole inbox into it, which reverses the order so the oldest element is on top. An element is poured **at most once** in its life.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- `push(x)`: `inbox.append(x)`.
- `pop()` / `peek()`: if `outbox` is empty, move every element of `inbox` to `outbox`; then pop or read the top of `outbox`.

**Amortized proof (accounting).** Charge 3 per push: 1 for pushing to the inbox, and 2 stored on the element to pay for its later move (pop from inbox, push to outbox). Pops cost 1. Each element is moved at most once, so stored credit always covers the pours.

**Potential version.** With $\Phi = 2\cdot|\text{inbox}|$, a pour of $m$ elements costs $2m$ and lowers $\Phi$ by $2m$, so its amortized cost is $O(1)$.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
#### Python

```{python}
#| label: cx-queue
class MyQueue:
    def __init__(self):
        self.inbox, self.outbox, self.moves = [], [], 0

    def push(self, x):
        self.inbox.append(x)

    def _pour(self):
        if not self.outbox:
            while self.inbox:
                self.outbox.append(self.inbox.pop())
                self.moves += 1

    def pop(self):
        self._pour()
        return self.outbox.pop()

    def peek(self):
        self._pour()
        return self.outbox[-1]

    def empty(self):
        return not self.inbox and not self.outbox

for _ in range(200):
    q, ref, pushes = MyQueue(), deque(), 0
    for _ in range(300):
        if ref and random.random() < 0.45:
            assert q.peek() == ref[0]
            assert q.pop() == ref.popleft()
        else:
            x = random.randint(0, 99)
            q.push(x); ref.append(x); pushes += 1
        assert q.empty() == (not ref)
    assert q.moves <= pushes            # each element is moved at most once
```

#### C++

```cpp
class MyQueue {
    stack<int> in, out;
    void pour() {
        if (out.empty())
            while (!in.empty()) { out.push(in.top()); in.pop(); }
    }
public:
    void push(int x) { in.push(x); }
    int pop() { pour(); int x = out.top(); out.pop(); return x; }
    int peek() { pour(); return out.top(); }
    bool empty() { return in.empty() && out.empty(); }
};
```
:::

::: {#fig-cx-queue}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    q = MyQueue()
    for x in (1, 2, 3):
        q.push(x)
    snaps = [("after push 1, 2, 3", list(q.inbox), list(q.outbox))]
    assert q.pop() == 1
    snaps.append(("after pop() → 1", list(q.inbox), list(q.outbox)))
    q.push(4)
    snaps.append(("after push 4", list(q.inbox), list(q.outbox)))
    for k, (title, inbox, outbox) in enumerate(snaps):
        x0 = k * 6.2
        V.stack(ax, p, inbox, x0, 0, title="inbox", color="indigo", w=1.4, top_label="")
        V.stack(ax, p, outbox, x0 + 2.6, 0, title="outbox", color="green", w=1.4, top_label="")
        V.text(ax, p, x0 + 2.0, 4.0, title, color="violet", size=10)
V.show(draw)
```

Push 1, 2, 3 go to the inbox. The first pop finds the outbox empty and pours the inbox into it, reversing the order, so 1 is on top. Later pushes wait in the inbox.

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Time** amortized $O(1)$ per operation; a single `pop` can be $O(n)$. **Space** $O(n)$.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- Pour **only** when the outbox is empty. Pouring on every pop breaks FIFO order and the amortized bound.
- Interleaved pushes and pops: new pushes wait in the inbox until the outbox drains, which keeps the order correct.
:::
